Subject: Thermodynamic interpolation and contact-wave controls

Independent primitive interpolation is a leading driver issue: native map n*v^2=C and T/v^2=D do not hold between vertices if n,T,v are interpolated separately. Source-band combined space/time samples give pressure p99 +28.8%, max +75.7%; native-spatial-node hourly time samples reach +101.4% pressure and +73.2% ram. These are sampled extrema, not upper bounds.

Separate optional corrected closure: interpolate speed, then n=C/v^2,T=D*v^2, then normalization scales, finally CME changes. C=1320464.1871439987,D=5.985098254241002 in cm^-3,km/s,K units. Defaultoff. 8000 CPU queries give max relative3.9e-16, bad-input rejection, default-off output identity, CME ordering tests pass. GPU gates underway. Parent sources preserved.

Balanced96 raw-driver controls (96x32x96, ±60,CFL.35): PN incident splitLLF1.75016e8,HLLE1.75474e8,HLLD1.49745e8 cm^-2s^-1. HLLD PN n3.359,v484.83, global fallback4183/21119acceptedsteps. Max point HLLD/HLLE flux28.0%; numerical convergence not established. HLLE/splitLLF maxpoint0.78%. Local conservative fallback experiment planned separately; no hidden floors.

Cached-next-CFL host/device synchronization derivative passes fullcoarse/freshshortwide identity; observed freshspeedup1.78x. Rawbalanced96 HLLD197s solve,132MB device,198MB hostpeak. With T scaled by 0.558 (ENLIL's effective p = (ρ/m_p)kT), the replica's speed bias against ENLIL drops from +30 to +4–9 km/s. That pins down the convention difference. What remains (r = 0.56–0.78 and density ×0.74–0.80 over a CME-heavy month) is typical inter-code spread from different dissipation (ENLIL is TVD-LF/HLL at 4°) and CME handling, and I'll report it as such. In production the DA anchors the 1 AU speeds, so the convention is second-order there. Waiting for the literature runs and the remaining queue.
